Error.description: An error, in the JSON error envelope.

Due.description: When a task is due: floating (the viewer's day) unless `tz` is set.

tz.description: Optional IANA time zone, only with `time`: the due is then the instant `date time` in that zone.

Error.description: Every error answer: a stable machine-readable code and an English message (docs/api.md, top).

code.description: A stable error code. New codes may be added in 1.x; treat an unknown one by its HTTP status.

message.description: A human-readable English message; do not parse it.

Field.description: field: a custom field definition of one project (OpenSpec change custom-fields, design D1). Like a section it lives in its project's sharing scope and project_id never changes after creation; type is fixed too (the REST API refuses a change). type is text|number|date|choice|link|checkbox, carried as a string so a later type is additive; options holds a choice field's options, one per line. Values live on the task as `fields.<id>`.

project_id.description: An id: a UUID, or for some entities a name-based id.

workspace_id.description: The workspace a field without a project belongs to (workspace-fields D1): an empty project_id makes the definition a workspace field that applies to every project of this workspace, before the projects' own fields. Null is the default workspace, as for a label. It lives in the author's personal scope and never changes after creation; it is ignored on a field with a project. Additive.

Label.description: task.labels holds label ids (a convention on the string array, not a format change).

group_by.description: Display options of the label's page (OpenSpec change list-display-options, design D1): grouping, order and direction, enumerations carried as strings like a view's; "" or an unknown value reads as the default. Labels are personal, so the choice follows the user to their own devices only.

manual_order.description: The label page's own manual order (OpenSpec change view-manual-order, design D1, D2): the ids of the tasks placed by hand, in order; tasks not listed follow by position. One whole-list register like view.panels, never a task's position. Not content.

row_layout.description: The label page's row layout (row-layouts D1); "" follows the account's.

workspace_id.description: Workspace of the label, null for the default (OpenSpec change workspaces).

Note.description: note: a standalone note (OpenSpec change notes-overview, design D1), not a task: it never shows in task lists, counts, calendars, filters or reminders. It lives in its project's sharing scope like a task, in the author's personal scope without a project (design D2). Its pending appends are the `appends.<id>` family.

day.description: A daily note's day, YYYY-MM-DD (daily-notes D1); "" for any other note. Set once at creation, only on the note whose id is the name-based id of its author and that day (NameID("daily-note", user + ":" + day)), so the same day is one note on every device.

labels.description: Label ids, one whole-list register like task.labels.

notes_doc.description: The note itself: Markdown in description, the mergeable document in notes_doc, written as a pair, as on tasks and projects.

position.description: Written at creation (the creation time) and kept for a later manual order; the Notes page sorts by when the note last changed.

project_id.description: The note's project, or null for a personal note; decides its scope.

template.description: A template (note-templates D1): the note is offered under From template… and New note copies it; otherwise a note like any other.

title.description: The note's title; an empty one reads "Untitled note".

workspace_id.description: The workspace of a note without a project, or null for the default; a note with a project follows its project, as task.workspace_id.

Objective.description: objective: one quarterly or weekly objective (OpenSpec change plan-objectives, design D1). Personal like place: it resolves to the author's personal scope, syncs to that user's devices only and derives no activity event. At most 5 open objectives per period: REST refuses a sixth, sync cannot refuse convergently and devices show all of them.

done_at.description: When it was marked done, Unix ms; 0 = open.

period.description: The quarter "YYYY-Qn" or ISO week "YYYY-Www" it is for; never a month.

title.description: The objective, one line of 1 to 140 characters (ciphertext for an encrypted account).

Origin.description: Where a task came from (docs/api.md "Task fields").

description.description: The project's note (OpenSpec change project-notes): Markdown in description, the mergeable document in notes_doc, as on tasks.

flow_mode.description: How the project's tasks flow (OpenSpec change project-flow-modes): "parallel", "sequential" or "area"; empty, missing or unknown reads as parallel. Sync checks the kind only, so a later value stays additive; REST and the agent tools check the set. Not user text.

icon.description: An icon name from the app's set, or null for the colour dot (OpenSpec change ux-overhaul, project-organization "Project icon"). Not user text, so it is not an encrypted content field.

notes_doc.description: A mergeable notes document ("ydoc:v1:…"), see docs/sync.md "Mergeable documents". Write `description` (Markdown) instead unless you merge documents yourself.

reusable.description: The reusable-list mode (OpenSpec change reusable-lists, design D1): adding an item already in the project reopens it instead of duplicating it, and ticked items always show. aisles sorts new items into aisle sections and reads as false while reusable is false. Flags, not user text, so not content; additive.

status.description: The project's status (OpenSpec change project-review-cadence, design D1): "active" or "maintenance"; empty, missing or unknown reads as active. Shared with the project's members and written by those who may change its other fields. Maintenance mutes the health words, the stalled marker and "without a next action"; a passed deadline still shows. Sync checks the kind only; REST and the agent tools check the set. Not user text.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the project belongs to, or null for the owner's default workspace (OpenSpec change workspaces, design D2). A partition key, not user text, so it is not an encrypted content field; on a shared project only the owner may write it (CanWrite).

Reminder.description: reminder: fires relative to its task's due time or at an absolute instant (OpenSpec change reminders, docs/sync.md). fire_at is always the resolved instant, recomputed by the device that changes the task's due; the server scheduler only compares it with the clock. delivered_at is written by the server (device "server") when a push went out.

fire_at.description: A point in time in Unix milliseconds.

offset_minutes.description: Minutes relative to the due time (negative: before).

radius_m.description: A location reminder's radius in metres, 100 to 5,000 (OpenSpec change location-reminders, design D1): set only on the kinds "arrive" and "leave", which fire on a phone that enters or leaves the circle around the task's location and never have a fire_at or an offset (reminder_check.go refuses the mixes). Not content: the place is in the task's encrypted location.

task_id.description: An id: a UUID, or for some entities a name-based id.

urgent.description: An urgent reminder (OpenSpec changes ios-urgent-alarms, design D1, and android-urgent-alarms): the iPhone and Android apps ring it as an alarm where they can; everywhere else it fires as an ordinary reminder. Not content.

Section.description: section: a named, ordered container inside one project (OpenSpec change board-view). It lives in the sharing scope of its project like a task does; project_id never changes after creation (Apply refuses a scope change, the REST API refuses any change).

aisle.description: The aisle an aisle section stands for in a reusable list (OpenSpec change reusable-lists, design D1): produce, bakery, dairy, meat, frozen, pantry, drinks, household or personal, or null. A fixed key, not user text, so it survives a rename and reads the same in every language; clients read an unknown key as null, and the REST API refuses it (invalid_aisle). Sync checks the kind only. Additive.

color.description: A palette colour (#rrggbb) and a name from the icon catalogue, or null (OpenSpec change icons-and-section-style, design D4–D5). Not user text, so neither is an encrypted content field. Sync checks the kind only: a newer client may write an icon this server does not know yet.

flow_mode.description: How the section's tasks flow (OpenSpec change project-flow-modes): "parallel" or "sequential"; empty, missing or unknown follows the project. Sync checks the kind only. Not user text.

project_id.description: An id: a UUID, or for some entities a name-based id.

assignee_id.description: Account id of the assignee or null (OpenSpec change task-assignment); additive. Apply checks it against the task scope's membership at receipt.

blocked_by.description: The tasks this one waits for, in its own sharing scope (OpenSpec change task-dependencies): one whole-list register; the resolver refuses ids of other scopes and lists that close a cycle.

completed_by.description: Account id of whoever completed the task, or null (OpenSpec change completed-date-filters, design D5); additive. Written beside completed_at; ApplyStrict fills it in for server-side completions.

day_part.description: The part of the day besides Evening (OpenSpec change day-parts, design D1): null, "morning" or "afternoon". Evening stays the evening flag; clients write both fields in one batch (D2), and a task with the flag set reads as Evening whatever this holds. Not content; additive.

deadline.description: The day the task must be finished by, separate from the planned due date (OpenSpec change deadlines); additive.

energy.description: The energy the task asks for (OpenSpec change task-energy, design D1): "" (none), "deep", "medium" or "low". Chosen from a menu, never written text, so not content (D2); additive.

estimate_minutes.description: Duration estimate in minutes (OpenSpec change nlp-quick-add); additive.

flow_mode.description: How the task's own subtasks flow (OpenSpec change subtask-flow, GitHub issue 1046): "sequential" offers its open subtasks one at a time in list order; empty, "parallel", missing or unknown read as parallel, as on a project. Sync checks the kind only, so a later value stays additive; a client that does not know it shows every subtask as available. Not user text, so not content.

habit.description: Habit tracking (habits D1): habit flags a series as a habit; skipped marks a record written by a skip. Additive booleans, not content.

habit_amount.description: habit-targets D2: the day's goal (0 none), the check button's step and the unit (content); the day's amount sums its habit_tally rows.

habit_color.description: The habit's own colour (OpenSpec change habits-polish, design D5): a palette hex such as "#22c55e", or "" for automatic (the project's colour, else one picked from the id). Not content, like project colours; additive.

habit_graduated_at.description: When the habit was graduated (habits-home D7), Unix ms, or null: a graduated habit is in no list, projection, reminder or Today limit and keeps its records; Resume continues it as a new piece of its lineage. Not content; additive.

habit_target.description: habit-targets D1: check-ins a period needs (0 none, at most 31) and the period ("", "week", "month"). Not content.

habit_tiny.description: The habit's tiny version and anchor (OpenSpec change habits-home, design D5): the two-minute version that still counts ("One page") and the moment it follows ("After dinner"). User-written text, so content; additive. Records copy them with the series' other fields, harmlessly.

ical_extra.description: Unmapped iCalendar content lines of the task's VTODO (OpenSpec change caldav, design D3): opaque text, stored and synced, never shown.

anyOf.description: Ciphertext on an end-to-end encrypted account.

location.description: Where the task happens (OpenSpec change task-locations): one whole-value register like origin, so concurrent locations never mix; additive.

note_mentions.description: The members an @mention in the notes names (OpenSpec change editor-everywhere, design D7): written with notes_doc, filtered to current members of the task's shared project at receipt, plaintext.

notes_doc.description: The note as a mergeable rich-text document (OpenSpec change collaborative-rich-text); additive. description stays its Markdown projection, written by clients in the same batch. Opaque here.

occurrence_date.description: The occurrence date an occurrence record stands for (OpenSpec change series-exceptions, design D1; iCalendar RECURRENCE-ID), kept when the record is moved. Written once with series_id; the resolver refuses it on a task without series_id and refuses a change once set. A date, not content; additive (a record without it stands for its due date).

anyOf.description: Ciphertext on an end-to-end encrypted account.

origin.description: Where the task came from (OpenSpec change task-origin): one whole-value register like due, so concurrent origins never mix; additive.

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule and the series an occurrence record belongs to (OpenSpec change recurring-tasks); additive. See docs/recurrence.md.

rotation.description: Who takes turns on a recurring task, in order (OpenSpec change chore-rotation; see rotation.go): plaintext member ids like assignee_id, not content; inert without a rule or a second member.

sample.description: A start guide sample task (moments-and-onboarding D3): excluded from Statistics, the Loop pulse and the digest. Not content; additive.

section_id.description: Section of the task's project or null (OpenSpec change board-view); additive. A reference to a deleted, foreign or unknown section is a display rule on clients ("No section"), never rejected on the sync path.

sector.description: The period the task is planned for without a date (OpenSpec change time-sectors, design D1): "" (none), an ISO week "2026-W44", a month "2026-11" or a quarter "2026-Q4". A sector with no do-on date schedules the task (it leaves the Inbox and Anytime) and is never overdue; clients name it relative to the viewer's date and derive carry-over, never writing it. A scheduling field like start: plaintext, not content; additive.

span.description: Draw the task as a span from its start date to its do-on date (OpenSpec change multi-day-tasks, design D1). Only drawing changes: start keeps deferring and due stays the do-on date, and a flag without a valid range (a date start before due.date) draws as a plain task. Not content; additive.

split_from.description: The series a piece of a split lineage continues and the date it starts (OpenSpec change series-split, design D2): {series, date}, one whole value. Set when the piece is created; the resolver refuses it on a task without a rule, with a series in another sharing scope, and as a change once set. Not content; additive (an older client sees an ordinary series).

start.description: When the task becomes relevant: a start date that defers it, or "someday" (parked); and the This Evening flag (OpenSpec change someday-and-evening); additive.

tiny.description: An occurrence record logged as the habit's tiny version (habits-home D5): set in the completion batch, never copied from the series; a full completion writes false. Not content; additive.

workspace_id.description: The workspace of a task without a project, or null for the default (OpenSpec change workspaces, design D2); a task with a project follows its project and this value is ignored there.

View.description: view: a saved filter query with presentation options (OpenSpec `custom-views`). kind, group_by, sort_by and sort_dir are enumerations carried as plain strings so a future option value stays additive: clients map unknown values to defaults at read time and only the REST API rejects them. panels holds view ids (dashboards).

card_notes.description: The Board layout's notes preview (OpenSpec change board-polish, design D4): each card shows two lines of its notes as plain text. A setting, not user text, so not content; missing reads as off.

icon.description: A name from the icon catalogue, or null for the default icon of the view's kind (OpenSpec change sidebar-polish, design D4). Not user text, so not content. Any string is accepted here so a newer catalogue stays additive; REST checks it with iconset.Valid and clients render an unknown name as the default icon.

layout.description: Display options of a list view (OpenSpec change views-and-display): the layout (an enumeration carried as a string), whether completed matches are listed, and the row properties the view hides.

manual_order.description: A list view's own manual order (OpenSpec change view-manual-order, design D1, D2): the ids of the tasks placed by hand, in order; tasks not listed follow by position. One whole-list register. Not content.

row_layout.description: The view's row layout (row-layouts D1): "line" or "detailed"; "" follows the account's choice (user_prefs.row_layout).

subtasks.description: Nest subtasks in the List layout (GitHub issue 1108): "nested" shows a match under its parent when both match, as Today's option does; "" or any other value is the flat list.

workspace_id.description: Workspace of the view, null for the default (OpenSpec change workspaces).

bearer.description: An API token. Scopes: full, read (refused on writes and sync), agent (writes only through the agent routes), admin, app (docs/api.md "Token scopes").

session.description: The browser session of the web app.

info.description: Every OpenTodo server serves this API under `/api/v1/` and this description at `/api/v1/openapi.json`. Authenticate with an API token (`Authorization: Bearer ot_…`, created in Settings → Integrations → API tokens) or a session cookie. Within 1.x the API only grows (docs/stability.md): ignore fields you do not know. Dates are floating `YYYY-MM-DD`, timestamps Unix milliseconds, priority 1 is the highest and 4 the default. One assistant turn drafts a routine with the one tool `draft_routine`; the model gets the steps available to you and the names and ids of your projects (not archived), their sections, labels, saved views and enabled webhooks (by host) as untrusted text. The draft (`{name, trigger, condition, steps}`, or `null` when the model answered in words, then in `note`) is checked like a create plus the draft rules (no task chosen by hand: no `get_task`, no `{"task": id}`; only available steps, else `unavailable`); when it does not check, the errors go back to the model once, and `errors` lists what still does not (`[{step?, input?, code, message}]`). Nothing is saved, enabled, tested or run, and a draft never holds `ai_apply`. `usage` is `{input, cached, cache_write, output, month_total, cap, own_key}` as for a turn; the tokens count toward the assistant allowance and `GET /api/v1/me/assistant/usage` lists them as `drafts`. `404 not_found` while the assistant is off, `409 encryption_enabled` for an encrypted account (it drafts on its device), `403 consent_required`, `413 too_large`, `429 assistant_quota` at the cap (with `resets_at`), `409 turn_in_progress` while another answer runs, `429 rate_limited` after 10 drafts in an hour, `422 ai_refused`/`ai_truncated`, provider errors as for a turn (`502`, `504 timeout`)

tags.description: An `agent` token may write through REST on this fixed list of routes only, and only while the owner's **Assistants may make changes** and the user's **Changes to my tasks** are both on:
tags.name: Agent tokens

tags.description: The OpenTodo app signs in through the system's authentication sheet (`ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, a Custom Tab on Android) with an authorization code and PKCE ([RFC 7636](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636), S256 only). The sheet shares the browser's cookies and passkeys, so every sign-in method of the web app works, and a browser that is already signed in only confirms. It does not depend on the owner's AI assistants (MCP) switch. A server that has it says so in `GET /api/v1/health` with `"app_sign_in": true`.
tags.name: App sign-in

tags.description: Attachments (OpenSpec `attachments`) are files or links on a task or one of its comments. Their metadata is an entity in the operation log (`attachment`, fields in [docs/sync.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/sync/#attachments)); the bytes are files moved with these routes. Every route answers `404 not_found` for an attachment or task you cannot read. Uploads need a session or a full token (`read` tokens get `403`) and are limited to 120 per hour per account (`429 rate_limited`).
tags.name: Attachments

tags.description: Rules (OpenSpec `automation-rules`; guide: [automations.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/automations/)) are the synced entity `rule`, personal like a label: `name` (content, encrypted for an encrypted account), `enabled`, `trigger`, `condition`, `actions`, `steps` (each one whole value), `position`, `created_at`, `deleted_at`. The app calls a rule a **routine**: a rule with `steps: null` is one Change tasks step with its `actions`; a routine of more than one step keeps them in `steps` (OpenSpec `routines-engine`, see [Routines](https://open-todo.app/docs/api/#routines)). Devices write them through `/api/v1/sync`; the REST routes below add id checks. The server runs them; their state (run log, watermarks, pauses) is server data, never operations. Every route answers `403 demo_restricted` on the public demo.
tags.name: Automation rules

tags.description: Other calendars shown in Day and Week, and your tasks as a calendar that calendar apps subscribe to (OpenSpec `calendar-feeds`). Everything here answers `404 feeds_disabled` while the owner's switch is off, and `403 demo_restricted` on the public demo. Read and agent tokens may use the `GET` routes only (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise).
tags.name: Calendar feeds

tags.description: Frames (OpenSpec `calendar-frames`; guide: [frames.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/frames/)) are the synced entity `frame`, personal like a rule: recurring background windows on the Day and Week grid such as "Deep work" on weekdays from 09:00 to 11:00. Fields: `title` (content, encrypted for an encrypted account), `weekdays` (ISO weekdays as a sorted comma list, `"1,2,3,4,5"`; 1 is Monday, 7 Sunday), `start` and `end` (floating wall times `HH:MM`, end after start), `color` (hex), `source` (the planning source: `""`, `project:<id>`, `label:<id>` or `view:<id>`), `from_date` and `until_date` (optional first and last day, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `position`, `created_at`, `deleted_at`. Occurrences are derived on the device and never stored. Devices write frames through `/api/v1/sync`; the REST routes below add the checks.
tags.name: Calendar frames

tags.description: Slots (OpenSpec `calendar-slots`; guide: [slots.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/slots/)) are the synced entity `slot`, personal like a frame: one block on the Day and Week grid that holds a checklist of small tasks, such as "Admin" on Wednesday from 16:00 for 45 minutes. Fields: `title` (content, encrypted for an encrypted account; empty reads as "Slot"), `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `start` (floating wall time `HH:MM`), `minutes` (15 to 480 in steps of 15; the op log accepts 1 to 1440), `task_ids` (ordered task ids, at most 20, written as one whole list), `color` (hex), `created_at`, `deleted_at`. No field is added to tasks: a task is in a slot when the slot lists it and the task is open and due on the slot's date without a time (or has no due date). Devices write slots through `/api/v1/sync`; the REST routes below add the checks.
tags.name: Calendar slots

tags.description: The account's own calendar (any CalDAV server with an app password, Google Calendar, or Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 through Microsoft Graph) receives its dated tasks as events, and changes made there come back to the tasks (OpenSpec change `calendar-two-way`; guide: [calendar-sync.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/calendar-sync/)). Every `/api/v1/calendar-sync` route answers `404 calendar_sync_disabled` while the owner's switch is off, and these routes and the settings answer `403 demo_restricted` on the public demo before authentication. Read and agent tokens may use the `GET` routes only. Connections are server data: never operations, never synced or exported; passwords, Google and Microsoft refresh tokens and the Google and Microsoft client secrets live in `<data>/secrets/calendar-sync.json` only and are never returned.
tags.name: Calendar sync

tags.description: The owner sets what a click on a task does for accounts that have not chosen (**Settings → Server → Task lists**): `select` (the first click selects the task, a second click on its title edits it) or `open` (a click opens the task). An account's own choice is the synced `user_prefs.row_click` (`select`, `open`, or `""` to follow the server) and always wins. `GET /api/v1/auth/status` carries `"rowClick": {"default": "select"}` for a signed-in caller.
tags.name: Click a task to

tags.description: For an account with end-to-end encryption, a device the user opted in answers the decrypt and encrypt steps of [MCP tool calls](https://open-todo.app/docs/mcp/#encrypted-accounts) (OpenSpec `mcp-device-relay`). The server never holds the key; relayed text exists only in memory during the call and is never stored, logged or audited. Session cookies only (no API tokens); every route is refused on a demo instance.
tags.name: Device relay

tags.description: A tenant of a host (see [host mode](https://open-todo.app/docs/self-hosting/host-mode/)) answers like any server, with these differences. `GET /api/v1/auth/status` adds `"hosted": true`. Settings that belong to the operator answer `403 host_managed` before authentication: `/api/v1/settings/smtp*`, `/api/v1/settings/oidc*` and `/api/v1/backups*` for every method, and writes to `/api/v1/settings/mcp`, `/api/v1/settings/assistant*`, `/api/v1/settings/webhooks` and `/api/v1/settings/attachments`.

tags.description: The [in-app assistant](https://open-todo.app/docs/assistant/) (OpenSpec `in-app-assistant`). Every route requires authentication. Settings, consent and usage are server state, never ops; conversations exist only on the device. Keys are write-only: no route ever returns one.

tags.description: GitHub and GitLab issues assigned to the account become tasks that follow the issue (OpenSpec `issue-connections`; guide: [issue-import.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/issue-import/)). Every `/api/v1/issues` route answers `404 issues_disabled` while the owner's switch is off, and these routes and the setting answer `403 demo_restricted` on the public demo before authentication. Read and agent tokens may use the `GET` routes only (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise). Connections are server data: never operations, never synced or exported.

tags.description: The owner of a project, or an admin of a shared one, can keep it and its sub-projects away from every AI assistant surface: MCP (whatever the token's scope), the agent content routes above and the in-app assistant then act as if it did not exist. Ordinary REST with a session, a `full` or an `admin` token, sync, CalDAV, feeds and the export are unaffected. It is server access state like membership: never an operation, never exported.

tags.description: The server proxies the map provider for the web app's maps and place search (guide: [locations and places](https://open-todo.app/docs/locations-and-places/)), so a browser never contacts a third party. The routes need a session or a `full` or `admin` token; with maps off they answer `404 maps_disabled`, and when the provider does not answer `502 maps_unavailable`. A demo instance has maps off unless `OPENTODO_MAPS=on`.
tags.name: Maps

tags.description: A person's delivery channels: ntfy, Pushover, Gotify, or a signed webhook (OpenSpec `notification-channels`; guide: [notification-channels.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/notification-channels/)). Every `/api/v1/notification-channels` route answers `404 channels_disabled` while the owner's switch is off; these routes and the setting answer `403 demo_restricted` on the public demo. Channels are server data: never operations, never synced or exported, and their tokens, user keys and signing secrets live in `<data>/secrets/notification-channels.json` only.
tags.name: Notification channels

tags.description: Every user changes their own name, email and picture. Profile data is server-side account data: never written to the op log, never synced. Members of shared projects see changes on their next sync. Changes are recorded as `account.name_changed`, `account.email_change_requested`, `account.email_changed` and `account.avatar_changed`, never with a name, an address or a picture.
tags.name: Profile

tags.description: A routine's `steps` is an ordered list of at most 20 steps (counted across blocks, at most 3 block levels, 32 KB): `{id, kind, in: {name: {ref} | {literal}}, then?, otherwise?, do?}`. `id` is 1 to 8 characters `a-z0-9`, unique (`trigger` and `item` are reserved); a `ref` names `trigger`, an earlier step visible from the step, or `item` inside a Repeat's `do`. The step kinds, their inputs and output types are listed by the catalogue route and in [routines.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/routines/#steps-and-values). Steps read tasks from the trigger or earlier steps: an input that takes one task (`add_comment.task`, `start_timer.task`, `notify.task`, `note_text.of`, `append_to_note.of`, `clear_note.of`, `create_tasks.parent`) and receives a list runs once per task (OpenSpec `routines-dynamic-data`). A task literal `{"task": id}` (on `add_comment`, `start_timer`, `notify` and `get_task`) is for rare fixed targets. `take` is Pick: `from` `start` (default), `end` or `all`, and `n` (default 1, ignored with `all`); `filter` is Pick's "where". `of` also takes `{"project": id}`. `date` outputs a Date (`date`: `today` by default, `tomorrow`, `{"in_days": n}` or `YYYY-MM-DD`); `project_of` outputs a task's project (the Inbox, an empty id, for a task without one); `create_tasks.parent` makes subtasks and refuses a `project` next to it; `split_lines.only: "open_checkboxes"` keeps only `- [ ] …` lines; `find_tasks` with a `query` or `view` finds completed tasks when the query names `completed` or `open` (a `condition` finds open tasks); in every form it never finds a task in the Trash or of a project in the Trash, and leaves out tasks of archived projects unless `archived` is `{"literal": true}` (OpenSpec `routines-find-scope`; the matching tasks of a `schedule` trigger with a condition follow the same rule). A `schedule` trigger takes `weekdays` or `month_days` (1 to 31 and `"last"`; a day a month lacks does not fire that month), exactly one; a condition may hold `unchanged: {days: 1..365}` (no field of the task changed in that many days). A routine is type-checked like the app does (`400 invalid_input` names the step and input, for example `step b: notify: text expects Text, got Tasks`), and every id inside it is resolved.
tags.name: Routines

tags.description: OpenSpec `routines-shared`; guide: [routines.md](https://open-todo.app/docs/routines/#routines-of-a-shared-project). The rule field `project_id` (null for a personal routine) makes a routine its project's: once the project is shared it lives in the project's scope like a task and syncs to every member. Owners, admins and editors write it; a viewer's operations are refused (`forbidden`, with the winning value back), and changing `project_id` across scopes is refused (`scope_change`). A shared project holds at most 50 routines; the per-account limit of 50 counts personal routines only (`409 limit_reached`). A create or patch is refused with `400 invalid_input` (*a shared routine acts only in its project: …*) when the trigger, condition or steps name another project, a task of another project or a move out of the project, and when they use labels or a webhook. Steps unavailable in a shared routine carry the reason `not_in_shared` (Favourite, Set today's focus, the timers, Tracked time, Create and Update project, a project from a template, Create labels, Email me, Send a webhook). The representation of a shared routine carries `run_as` (`{id, name}`: the author of the winning `enabled: true`, null before anyone turned it on) and, when someone else's edit paused it, `paused_by`; `GET /api/v1/me/rules` gives both per rule. Its event, schedule, due and overdue runs see only the project, act as `run_as` (role checked before each run and at writing, device `rule:<rule-id>`), fire on any member's changes to the project's tasks, and pause with `paused_reason` `edited_by_other` (someone else changed `trigger`, `condition`, `steps`, `actions`, `ai_apply` or `ai_budget`), `run_as_viewer` or `run_as_left` (the owner, admins and editors get a `routine_paused_shared` notification, `{ruleId, ruleName, projectId, projectName, runAsName, reason, at}`). `POST …/run` (also with `test`) runs as the caller and answers a viewer `403 forbidden`; the draft test takes `project_id` to plan inside a project. Every member reads the runs (`project_id` on each run; a non-member gets `404 not_found`); `POST …/undo` needs editor or above (`403 forbidden`). `ai_mode.reason` is `not_run_as` when Apply without asking was turned on by someone other than `run_as`.
tags.name: Routines of a shared project

tags.description: A section is a named, ordered container inside one project (OpenSpec change `board-view`): a heading in the list view and a column on the board. Sections are soft-deleted like everything else, live in the sharing scope of their project (editors and up may write them, viewers read them) and appear in the export, deleted ones included.
tags.name: Sections

tags.description: The owner sets the default light and dark theme of the server and offers up to 20 server themes to everyone (**Settings → Server → Branding**). A member whose choice for a side is empty sees the server default; a member's own choice always wins, and nothing is written to anyone's data. `GET /api/v1/auth/status` carries `"themes": {"version": 3}` for a signed-in caller; the version grows with every change, so a device reads the themes again when it differs from the one it has.
tags.name: Server themes

tags.description: Voice capture sends a recorded phrase through the server to the owner's OpenAI-compatible transcription service (guides: [speech to text](https://open-todo.app/docs/self-hosting/speech-to-text/), [quick add](https://open-todo.app/docs/quick-add/)). The audio and the text stay in memory for the request: never stored, logged or audited. `GET /api/v1/me` carries `speech: {connected, host?}` for every user.
tags.name: Speech to text

tags.description: A workspace is a separate room with its own projects, labels, views and people (OpenSpec `workspaces`, guide: [workspaces](https://open-todo.app/docs/workspaces/)). Every account has one default workspace (`"default": true`, named "Personal" until renamed), which cannot be deleted, left, transferred or given members (409 `default_workspace`). Projects, labels, views and tasks without a project carry `workspace_id` (null or absent = the default workspace; a task with a project follows its project); on a shared project only the owner may change it. Workspaces, members and groups are server data, never ops; every sync response carries `workspaces` (below).
